stem: What is meant by the allocation of an overhead?

options.content: Charging the whole cost to the cost centre that incurred it
options.rationale: Correct: the cost belongs wholly to that centre.

options.content: Sharing a cost among several cost centres on a fair basis
options.rationale: That is apportionment.

options.content: Sharing service department costs among production departments
options.rationale: That is reapportionment.

options.content: Adding overheads to the cost of each unit
options.rationale: That is absorption.

explanation: Allocation charges a whole, identifiable cost to one cost centre, for example the salary of the assembly supervisor to the assembly department.

stem: Which basis is most suitable for apportioning the rent of a factory building among departments?

options.content: Floor area
options.rationale: Correct: a department uses rent in proportion to the space it occupies.

options.content: Number of employees
options.rationale: Employees are a basis for the canteen or personnel costs, not rent.

options.content: Machine hours
options.rationale: Machine hours suit power or machine running costs.

options.content: Value of materials issued
options.rationale: That is a basis for stores costs.

explanation: Rent is caused by space, so floor area (or volume) is used.

stem: Which basis is most suitable for apportioning the depreciation of machinery?

options.content: Floor area of each department in square metres
options.rationale: Floor area is unrelated to the value of the machines.

options.content: Number of employees working in each department
options.rationale: Employees do not cause depreciation of machines.

options.content: Carrying amount of the machinery in each department
options.rationale: Correct: the larger the machines used, the larger the depreciation.

options.content: Direct labour hours worked in each department
options.rationale: Hours of labour are not the cause of machine depreciation.

explanation: Depreciation arises from the machines, so the cost or carrying amount of machinery in each department is the best basis.

stem: Rent of US\$18,000 is to be shared on floor area. Department X has 400 m², Y has 300 m² and Z has 100 m². How much is apportioned to Y?

options.rationale: This shares the rent equally and ignores the floor areas.
This is the share of X, the largest department.
This uses 700 m² as the total, leaving out department Z.

stem: After the service department costs have been fully reapportioned, which statement about the overhead analysis sheet is correct?

options.content: The service departments keep their own costs for use as an overhead rate
options.rationale: Service departments make no product to absorb into.

options.content: The total overhead is lower than before reapportionment
options.rationale: Reapportionment moves cost between departments; the total does not change.

options.content: The production departments carry only the allocated costs
options.rationale: They carry allocated, apportioned and reapportioned costs.

options.content: The service departments show nil and the production departments carry the whole overhead
options.rationale: Correct: only production departments absorb overheads into products.

explanation: Reapportionment moves the service departments' costs to the production departments. The grand total is unchanged.
hints: Think of reapportionment as moving cost, not removing it.

stem: Which overhead of a factory with several departments would normally be allocated and not apportioned?

options.content: Insurance of the whole factory building
options.rationale: It benefits all departments, so it is apportioned.

options.content: Pay of the painting department's supervisor
options.rationale: Correct: the cost belongs wholly to one department.

options.content: Heating and lighting of the whole factory
options.rationale: It is shared, so it is apportioned on floor area.

options.content: Cost of the factory's security guard at the gate
options.rationale: The guard serves the whole factory: apportioned.

explanation: A cost that can be identified wholly with one department is allocated; shared costs are apportioned.
hints: Does the cost belong to one department only?

stem: A manager apportions the power cost on floor area although most power is used by one heavily mechanised department with a small floor space. What is the likely effect?

options.content: The total overhead of the whole factory will be understated
options.rationale: The total is the same whatever the basis.

options.content: Its overhead is overstated because of the small floor space
options.rationale: The small floor area gives it a small share, so it is understated.

options.content: Its overhead is understated and its products look too cheap
options.rationale: Correct: the department that causes most of the power gets too little of its cost.

options.content: The cost of products from other departments will fall
options.rationale: They absorb more of the cost, so their products look more expensive.

explanation: The basis decides who carries the cost. Using area gives the high-power department too little, so its products are under-costed and the others over-costed.
hints: Compare the share of floor area with the share of power used.

stem: The total overhead of a factory changes when service department costs are reapportioned to production departments.
explanation: False. Reapportionment only moves cost between departments; the total stays the same.

stem: A cost may be apportioned on a different basis from year to year and the resulting product costs may change, even if the total overhead is the same.
explanation: True. The basis decides how the total is shared among departments, so it changes product costs.

stem: Match each overhead to the most suitable basis of apportionment.
explanation: Space-related costs use floor area; machine-related costs use machinery value; canteen costs use employees; power uses machine hours or meter readings.

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: Sharing the cost of a service department among production departments is called {{blank:a}}. A department that makes no product, such as maintenance, is a {{blank:b}} department.

explanation: Reapportionment moves service department costs to production departments; maintenance and the canteen are service departments.

stem: Name the schedule on which allocated and apportioned overheads are recorded for each department.
explanation: It is the overhead analysis sheet.

stem: Insurance of machinery of US\$7,500 is apportioned on the carrying amount of machinery: Department A US\$48,000, Department B US\$32,000 and the Stores US\$20,000. Calculate the amount apportioned to Department B.
explanation: 7,500 × 32,000/100,000 = US\$2,400. Dividing by the production departments only (80,000) would ignore the Stores.
workedSolution: 1. 7,500 × 32,000/100,000 = US\$2,400. Dividing by the production departments only (80,000) would ignore the Stores.

stem: After allocation and apportionment, the stores department has total overheads of US\$13,200. Its services are used by the Cutting and Finishing departments in the ratio 55% : 45%. Calculate the cost reapportioned to Cutting.
explanation: 13,200 × 55% = US\$7,260. Finishing receives US\$5,940.
hints: Multiply the stores total by the percentage for Cutting.

stem: The total overheads of Cutting are US\$41,800 before reapportionment. Using the reapportionment of the stores costs in the previous question, calculate the total overhead of the Cutting department after reapportionment.
explanation: 41,800 + 7,260 = US\$49,060. Check: Finishing = 27,300 + 5,940 = 33,240; together 82,300 equals the original total.
workedSolution: 1. 41,800 + 7,260 = US\$49,060. Check: Finishing = 27,300 + 5,940 = 33,240; together 82,300 equals the original total.
hints: Add the share of the stores cost.

stem: Distinguish between allocation and apportionment of overheads.

points.description: Allocation charges a whole cost to the one cost centre that caused it
Apportionment shares a cost that benefits several cost centres among them on a suitable basis

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Allocation charges a whole cost to one cost centre; apportionment divides a shared cost among several cost centres using a basis such as floor area.

explanation: One mark for each correct definition.

stem: Explain why the cost of the canteen is reapportioned to production departments and not absorbed directly into the cost of products.

points.description: The canteen makes no product and so has no output to which cost can be charged
Its cost is a necessary part of the cost of production because it supports the workers
Reapportioning to production departments lets the cost be absorbed in their rates

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The canteen does not make a product. Its cost helps production, so it is shared among the production departments and then absorbed in their overhead rates.

explanation: One mark for each point.
hints: Which departments make the goods that are sold?

stem: A factory apportions rent on floor area and power on floor area. Evaluate whether this is suitable.

points.description: Floor area is a suitable basis for rent because space causes the cost
It is not suitable for power if departments use machines of different size or running time
Using machine hours or meter readings would better reflect the power used
A poor basis misstates departmental costs and the cost and price of products

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Floor area suits rent but not power, which depends on machine use. Machine hours or meters would give a fairer split. A poor basis gives wrong department costs and so wrong product costs and selling prices.

explanation: One mark for each point.

stem:
Bulawayo Plastics Ltd has two production departments, Moulding and Finishing, and a Stores department. Overheads for the year ended 31 December 2025:

| Overhead | US\$ | Basis or allocation |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Factory rent | 20,000 | Floor area: Moulding 400 m², Finishing 350 m², Stores 250 m² |
| Depreciation of machinery | 15,000 | Carrying amount: Moulding 50%, Finishing 30%, Stores 20% |
| Power | 7,800 | Kilowatt hours: 8, 3 and 1 parts |
| Supervisors' salaries | 7,900 | Moulding US\$4,200; Finishing US\$3,700 |
| Storekeepers' wages | 6,400 | Stores |

The Stores department is used by Moulding and Finishing in the ratio 60 : 40.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the rent apportioned to Moulding.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the power apportioned to Finishing.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the total overhead of the Stores department before reapportionment.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the total overhead of the Moulding department after reapportioning the Stores department.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: What is the total overhead of Finishing after reapportionment, and what is the grand total of the two production departments?

options.content: Finishing US\$17,150; grand total US\$42,050
options.rationale: This ignores the reapportionment of Stores.

options.content: Finishing US\$32,200; grand total US\$66,130
options.rationale: This charges all of the stores cost to Finishing.

options.content: Finishing US\$23,170; grand total US\$48,070
options.rationale: This leaves out Moulding's share of the stores cost.

options.content: Finishing US\$23,170; grand total US\$57,100
options.rationale: Correct: the grand total equals all the overheads.

explanation: This item tests apportionment, allocation and the reapportionment of a service department.
hints: Check that the department totals equal the total of all overheads.

stem:
Mutare Milling Ltd has production departments Milling and Packing and service departments Maintenance and Canteen. After allocation and apportionment, the overheads for 2025 are:

| Department | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Milling | 32,400 |
| Packing | 19,600 |
| Maintenance | 9,600 |
| Canteen | 6,000 |

The canteen is used by Milling, Packing and Maintenance employees in the ratio 8 : 6 : 6. Maintenance serves only the production departments, in the ratio 60 : 40. The canteen is reapportioned first.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the canteen cost reapportioned to Maintenance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the total of the Maintenance department to be reapportioned.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the final total overhead of:

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why the canteen was reapportioned before Maintenance and state the check that proves both reapportionments are complete.

points.description: The canteen serves Maintenance, so its cost must be added to Maintenance before Maintenance is shared out
Maintenance does not serve the canteen, so no cost is returned to the canteen
Check: the final totals of the two production departments (41,640 + 25,960) equal the original total of 67,600
The service departments show nil after reapportionment

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The canteen serves Maintenance, so its cost is added to Maintenance first and then Maintenance is cleared in full. The total of Milling and Packing 67,600 equals the original total 67,600, and both service departments are nil.

explanation: This item uses a step-down reapportionment with a service department serving another.
hints: Maintenance receives part of the canteen cost.
The grand total does not change.
